fodele.name: Fodele Beach
fodele.description: Fodele Beach is a sandy beach located just a few kilometers north of Fodele village, about 25 km west of Heraklion. It has golden sand, clear waters, and is surrounded by green hills, giving it a more natural, peaceful feel. The beach is partly organized, with sunbeds, umbrellas, and a few cafes nearby.

agiaPelagia.name: Agia Pelagia
agiaPelagia.description: Agia Pelagia Beach is a popular seaside spot located about 20 km west of Heraklion. It's set in a beautiful, sheltered bay, with calm, crystal-clear waters and soft golden sand — perfect for swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing. The beach is well-organized with sunbeds, umbrellas, and lots of cafes and tavernas.

paliokastro.name: Paliokastro
paliokastro.description: Paliokastro is a small coastal area located about 15 km west of Heraklion. It's known for its rocky landscape, small pebbly beach, and the ruins of a Venetian fortress. The beach has deep, clear waters — great for swimming, snorkeling, and diving — but it's wilder and more natural compared to organized tourist beaches.

sisi.name: Sissi
sisi.description: Sissi is a small, peaceful fishing village on the northeastern coast of Crete. It's about 35 km east of Heraklion and close to Malia. Known for its charming harbor, small sandy beaches, and relaxed atmosphere, it's a perfect escape from the more crowded tourist destinations.

matala.name: Matala
matala.description: Matala is a picturesque village on the southern coast of Crete, about 75 km southwest of Heraklion. It's famous for its sandy beach, clear turquoise waters, and the iconic caves carved into the cliffs, which were once used by ancient Minoans and later became home to hippies in the 1960s.

lentas.name: Lentas
lentas.description: Lentas is a quiet, charming village on the southern coast of Crete, about 75 km south of Heraklion. It's known for its peaceful vibe, beautiful sandy and pebbly beach, and scenic views of the Asterousia Mountains. Historically a harbor for the ancient city of Gortyn.

threeChurches.name: Three Churches
threeChurches.description: Three Churches is a small, remote coastal area in southern Crete — a hidden gem offering stunning natural beauty, secluded beaches, and a peaceful atmosphere. The landscaped surroundings make it a perfect spot for those looking to escape the urban environment.

tsoutsouros.name: Tsoutsouros
tsoutsouros.description: Tsoutsouros is a small, peaceful village on the southern coast of Crete, about 65 km south of Heraklion. Known for its long sandy beach and crystal-clear waters, it's perfect for swimming and relaxing. The area is also historically significant, with nearby ruins of the ancient city of Inatos.

knossosPalace.name: Knossos Palace
knossosPalace.description: The largest Bronze Age archaeological site on Crete, associated with the myth of the Minotaur and the Labyrinth. Dating from around 2000-1400 BC, it showcases advanced Minoan architecture, colorful frescoes, and storied mythology. The most famous Minoan palace in the world.

koulesForetress.name: Koules Fortress
koulesForetress.description: A 16th-century Venetian fortress at the entrance to Heraklion's old harbor. It offers panoramic sea views and insight into Venetian maritime defense. A landmark of Heraklion and a great spot to enjoy the sunset over the sea.

archaeologicalMuseum.name: Archaeological Museum
archaeologicalMuseum.description: One of the most significant museums in Greece for Minoan artifacts. Must-see items include the Phaistos Disc, Snake Goddess figurines, and frescoes from Knossos. It perfectly complements a visit to Knossos Palace.

agiosTitos.name: Church of Agios Titos
agiosTitos.description: Originally built in the 10th century and reconstructed in the 19th century, this beautifully restored church reflects Crete's layered religious history with a mix of Byzantine, Venetian, and Ottoman architectural influences.

bali.name: Bali
bali.description: Bali is a charming seaside village on the north coast of Crete, known for its beautiful beaches with calm, clear waters, ideal for swimming and relaxing. Surrounded by hills and olive groves, it offers a blend of nature and tradition — great for families, couples, and anyone seeking a quiet beach getaway.

georgioupoli.name: Georgioupoli
georgioupoli.description: Georgioupoli is a charming coastal village on the northwest coast of Crete, famous for its long sandy beach stretching over 10 kilometers and its beautiful Almyros River. The iconic small white chapel of Agios Nikolaos, built on a rocky islet, is a must-see.

preveli.name: Preveli
preveli.description: Preveli is a famous beach on the south coast of Crete, best known for its unique palm forest where the Kourtaliotis River flows into the sea, creating a beautiful lagoon. Above the beach sits the historic Preveli Monastery. Perfect for nature lovers and hikers.

plakias.name: Plakias
plakias.description: Plakias is a relaxed seaside village on the south coast of Crete, famous for its wide sandy beach, beautiful mountain backdrop, and laid-back atmosphere. The crystal-clear waters are perfect for swimming, snorkeling, and windsurfing. Nearby you can visit Preveli Beach and Kourtaliotiko Gorge.

elafonisi.name: Elafonisi
elafonisi.description: Elafonisi is a small island and beach on the southwest coast of Crete, famous for its pink sand and crystal-clear, shallow waters. The sand gets its pink color from crushed seashells. You can walk through the shallow water to reach the island — one of the most beautiful beaches in Greece.

balos.name: Balos Lagoon
balos.description: Balos Lagoon is one of the most stunning natural sights in Crete, located on the northwest coast near Kissamos. It's famous for its shallow turquoise waters, white-pink sand, and incredible lagoon landscape. You can reach it by boat or by driving and hiking down a rocky path.

falasarna.name: Falasarna
falasarna.description: Falasarna is a beautiful beach area on the west coast of Crete, near Kissamos. It's famous for its long, wide sandy beach, clear blue waters, and amazing sunsets. The beach is made up of several smaller beaches, giving it a natural, open feel. Ancient ruins of a Greek-Roman city are nearby.

stavros.name: Stavros (Zorba Beach)
stavros.description: Stavros is a small, quiet coastal village on the Akrotiri Peninsula, about 15-20 km northeast of Chania. It's famous for its beautiful circular beach with shallow turquoise waters and a dramatic rocky mountain. This is where the famous movie "Zorba the Greek" (1964) was filmed.

elounda.name: Elounda
elounda.description: Elounda is a beautiful coastal town in northeastern Crete, famous for its calm blue waters, luxurious resorts, and relaxed atmosphere. Originally a fishing village, it has become one of Crete's top destinations. Nearby you can visit the famous Spinalonga Island with its Venetian fortress.

voulisma.name: Voulisma (Golden Beach)
voulisma.description: Voulisma Beach is one of the most beautiful beaches in eastern Crete, near the village of Istro. It's famous for its bright turquoise waters, soft golden sand, and tropical vibe. The water is shallow and very clear, making it ideal for swimming and snorkeling.

vai.name: Vai Palm Beach
vai.description: Vai Beach is famous for its huge natural palm forest — the largest in Europe. The beach has golden sand, clear turquoise waters, and a tropical, exotic feel. A well-organized beach that still feels natural and special thanks to the impressive palm forest surrounding it.

makrigialos.name: Makrigialos
makrigialos.description: Makrigialos is a peaceful seaside village on the southeast coast of Crete. It's known for its long sandy beach, calm shallow waters, and relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere. The name means "long beach" in Greek! It has a charming harbor and seafront tavernas.
